questions.sub: Physical geography of India: relief, drainage, climate
questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak in India?
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), on the India-Nepal border in Sikkim, is the highest peak located within India; K2 lies in Pakistan-administered territory.

questions.sub: Physical geography of India: relief, drainage, climate
questions.question: The river Brahmaputra is known as which name in Tibet before entering India?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet as the Tsangpo, enters India through Arunachal Pradesh (as the Dihang/Siang), and flows through Assam.

questions.question: The southwest monsoon typically first hits the Indian mainland at which coast?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon typically makes its onset over the Kerala coast around the first week of June, then advances further into the mainland.

questions.question: The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from India typically begins from which region?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon begins its withdrawal from West Rajasthan (northwest India) around early September.

questions.question: Which soil type, found extensively in the Deccan Plateau and formed from weathered basaltic lava, is well suited for cotton cultivation?
questions.explanation: Black soil (regur soil), derived from Deccan Trap basaltic rocks, has high moisture-retention capacity and is ideal for cotton, hence also called 'black cotton soil'.

questions.question: India's largest reserves of iron ore are found predominantly in which state?
questions.explanation: Odisha holds the largest share of India's iron ore reserves, along with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand as other major producers.

questions.question: The 'Rabi' crops in India are sown around which season and harvested in spring?

options.A: Sown in June-July (onset of monsoon), harvested in September-October
options.B: Sown in October-December (winter), harvested in March-April
options.D: Sown in April-May, harvested in July-August

questions.explanation: Rabi crops (e.g., wheat, barley, mustard) are sown in winter (October-December) and harvested in spring (March-April).

questions.question: As per the 2011 Census, which Indian state/UT recorded the highest population density?
questions.explanation: Among states, Bihar had the highest density in the 2011 Census, but overall Delhi (a Union Territory) recorded the highest population density in the country.

questions.question: Which is the longest National Highway in India, connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari?
questions.explanation: NH 44 (formerly NH 7), running from Srinagar to Kanyakumari, is the longest national highway in India.

questions.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
questions.question: Mizoram is bordered internationally by which two countries?
questions.explanation: Mizoram shares international borders with Bangladesh to the west and Myanmar to the east and south.

questions.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
questions.question: Which is the largest and most important river of Mizoram, flowing from Myanmar through the south of the state before re-entering Myanmar?
questions.explanation: The Kolodyne (locally Chhimtuipui) is the largest and most important river of Mizoram, flowing from Myanmar through the south of the state before re-entering Myanmar.

questions.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
questions.question: As of the reorganisation completed in 2019, how many districts does Mizoram have?
questions.explanation: Mizoram has 11 districts (following the 2019 reorganisation which created new districts such as Khawzawl, Saitual and Hnahthial in addition to the original 8).

questions.sub: Geography of Mizoram: location, relief, rivers, climate, districts
questions.question: Which is the capital and largest city of Mizoram, located on a ridge in Aizawl district?
questions.explanation: Aizawl, situated on a ridge at an average elevation of about 1,132 metres, is the capital and largest city of Mizoram.

questions.sub: Disaster-prone zones, seismic zonation of the North East
questions.question: As per the seismic zonation map of India, the entire North Eastern region, including Mizoram, falls under which seismic zone?
questions.explanation: The entire North Eastern region of India, including Mizoram, lies in Seismic Zone V, the zone of highest earthquake risk as per the Bureau of Indian Standards classification.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of the following Indian states?

options.B: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram

questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees N) passes through eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
